⚡ Quick Analysis

Capital budget bill for fire protection infrastructure. Direct fiscal impact through state construction budget. No direct ATM/retail business impact unless your locations are in areas receiving fire station upgrades (indirect property value effect).

✅ Proponents
Fire districts, local governments, construction unions
❌ Opponents
Fiscal conservatives (spending concerns)
⚖️ Watchers
Taxpayer groups, environmental (water use)
Prefiled
First Reading
Committee
Floor Vote
Senate
Governor
Bill Summary

HB 1001 authorizes capital projects for fire protection services across Washington State. This is a standard capital budget appropriation bill that funds construction, renovation, and equipment acquisition for fire districts and fire protection authorities.

Key Provisions
  • Capital appropriations for fire station construction/renovation
  • Equipment acquisition (apparatus, communications)
  • Grants to local fire districts
  • Bond financing authorization
Fiscal Impact

State: Bond issuance + general fund appropriations. Exact amount TBD in committee.
Local: Matching requirements for districts receiving grants.
Private Sector: Construction contracts bid out; opportunity for contractors.

Stakeholder Positions (Detailed)
  • Washington State Fire Fighters Union Strong Support
  • Association of Washington Cities Support
  • Washington State Association of Counties Support
  • Building Industry Association of WA Support (contracts)
  • WA Policy Center (fiscal conservative) Oppose (spending)
Political Dynamics

House: Democratic majority (58-40). Bill has bipartisan sponsors (3R, 3D). Likely passes committee along party lines or with bipartisan support.

Senate: Democratic majority (29-20). Similar trajectory expected.

Governor: Ferguson (D) likely signs; fire protection is non-controversial constituency service.

Business Impact Assessment

Direct: None for ATM/payments industry.
Indirect: Fire station construction may cause temporary road closures near your ATM locations. Property value increases in served areas could affect retail foot traffic.
Opportunity: If you have construction sector clients, they may bid on these projects.

Amendment Watch

No amendments filed yet. Watch for:
- Geographic allocation changes (rural vs urban)
- Matching fund ratio adjustments
- Environmental review requirements added

Vote Projection
House (Projected)
~65 Yes / 35 No / 0 Absent
Senate (Projected)
~60 Yes / 40 No / 0 Absent
Action Items

✅ No action needed — This bill has no direct impact on Forza Payments or ATM operations.
📌 Monitor only if you have retail locations in areas with active fire station construction.
